{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-3h3a","title":"rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs: MSB matching panics when shift equals u128 bit width","description":"In rule_matches(), when Mo::Msb is used with mo_arg = 0 and fd.length_bits = 128 (a full IPv6 address), the calculation `shift = fd.length_bits - mo_arg` yields 128. The subsequent `val >> shift` panics in debug builds because shifting a u128 by 128 bits is an overflow. The guard on line 184 only rejects mo_arg > length_bits, not the case where shift >= 128.

Fix suggestion: Add an early-out check: `if mo_arg == 0 { /* comparing 0 MSBs always matches */ }` before the shift, or clamp shift to 127 max. Alternatively, use wrapping_shr or checked_shr to avoid the panic.
